summary: This article explains how heat and cold change water between ice and liquid, why ice expands and floats, and how other materials melt at their own temperatures.
introduce: Show the three key terms on the board and ask students to rate each one: “I know it,” “I have seen it,” or “It is new.” Tell them to watch for these words in “Freezing and Melting” and use clues around them to understand their meaning.

keyTerms.def: how hot or cold something is
a very tiny piece of something
able to be changed back to how it was before

challengeTerms.def: the smallest bit of a substance that is still that substance
a solid whose tiny parts are arranged in a neat, repeating pattern
to take in something, such as heat, light, or liquid

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that water is the most interesting material on Earth? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain what happens to the particles in water when it freezes and when it melts.
struggling: Pre-teach temperature, particle, and reversible with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers draw a quick picture for each term and use it in a short spoken sentence.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses molecule, crystal, and absorb to teach the class one of the terms with their own example.
